tools.name: list_devices
tools.description: Find attached iOS devices and booted or previously used simulators. Set include_all_simulators to also show shutdown simulators and available models. Every other device tool needs one of these ids as device. When exactly one device is listed, default names it.

tools.name: start_simulator
tools.description: Boot an existing simulator by id or name, or create one from an available model. Prepare accessibility before boot and return its id; pass that id as device to later calls. A simulator already listed by list_devices can also be used directly: any call that names it boots it.

tools.name: shut_down_simulator
tools.description: Shut down the simulator named by device. This operation does not power off physical devices.

device.description: The device to act on: its id from list_devices (or its exact name).

tools.name: get_device_info
tools.description: Read device identity, capture dimensions in logical points, and optionally platform settings. Missing or unsupported settings remain visible in the result.

device.description: The device to act on: its id from list_devices (or its exact name).

tools.name: take_screenshot
tools.description: Capture the current display and return a JPEG image with screen dimensions and a prompt warning check. max_width resizes the image only; interaction coordinates remain logical points. The compatibility lossless argument does not change this JPEG response.

device.description: The device to act on: its id from list_devices (or its exact name).

tools.name: save_screenshot
tools.description: Save a full-resolution screenshot to an absolute PNG or JPEG path or directory. The file extension controls encoding. Existing files require overwrite=true; the default directory is Pictures/Poki MCP. The compatibility lossless argument does not override the extension.

device.description: The device to act on: its id from list_devices (or its exact name).

tools.name: start_recording
tools.description: Start recording the device display to an H.264 movie. One recording is retained per device in this session; requires ffmpeg and ffprobe.

device.description: The device to act on: its id from list_devices (or its exact name).

tools.name: stop_recording
tools.description: Finalize this session's recording of the device and inspect the saved movie before returning its path and media details.

device.description: The device to act on: its id from list_devices (or its exact name).

tools.name: get_foreground_app
tools.description: Read the current foreground application from accessibility services. A missing bundle identifier may be null; no app is inferred from launch history.

device.description: The device to act on: its id from list_devices (or its exact name).

tools.name: list_elements
tools.description: Read accessibility elements, or OCR when auto mode cannot use accessibility. When accessibility names nothing across a third of the screen, auto mode adds the screenshot text it did not name, each marked source ocr. Return logical-point frames and short-lived element refs. Refresh refs after input or screen changes. max_elements defaults to 400.

device.description: The device to act on: its id from list_devices (or its exact name).

tools.name: tap
tools.description: Tap at x/y in screen points or at the center of a current element ref. Refresh refs with list_elements after input; ambiguous or stale targets are rejected. sent=true only means the touch was written to the device. screen_change compares what accessibility reports before and after the tap: the elements, their text, values, selected/enabled/focused state and positions. It is changed, unchanged, or unknown when the screen could not be compared in time (unknown is not a failure). unchanged is not proof the tap failed (an effect on a canvas or image, or one that arrives late, is not seen); the reply says so in instruction.

device.description: The device to act on: its id from list_devices (or its exact name).

verify.description: Set false to skip action verification. Returns verified:false. Text targeting and coordinate sizing still read current device data.

tools.name: tap_text
tools.description: Find one visible element matching text, waiting up to five seconds for it to appear and hold still, trying OCR when needed, and tap it. Returns the visible text afterwards and screen_change. sent=true only means the touch was written to the device, which does not acknowledge it. screen_change compares what accessibility reports before and after the tap: the elements, their text, values, selected/enabled/focused state and positions. It is changed, unchanged, or unknown when the screen could not be compared in time (unknown is not a failure). unchanged is not proof the tap failed (an effect on a canvas or image, or one that arrives late, is not seen); the reply says so in instruction. Multiple matches produce an error without tapping; a missing target reports the closest text on screen.

device.description: The device to act on: its id from list_devices (or its exact name).

verify.description: Set false to skip action verification. Returns verified:false. Text targeting and coordinate sizing still read current device data.

tools.name: double_tap
tools.description: Send two taps at x/y in logical screen points or at a current element ref. Read back the screen to confirm the intended effect.

device.description: The device to act on: its id from list_devices (or its exact name).

tools.name: long_press
tools.description: Hold one touch at x/y or an element ref. duration is in seconds and defaults to one second. Coordinates use logical screen points.

device.description: The device to act on: its id from list_devices (or its exact name).

tools.name: swipe
tools.description: Move a touch from from_x/from_y to to_x/to_y in logical screen points. duration_ms defaults to 300. Inspect the resulting screen after delivery.

device.description: The device to act on: its id from list_devices (or its exact name).

verify.description: Set false to skip action verification. Returns verified:false. Text targeting and coordinate sizing still read current device data.

tools.name: scroll
tools.description: Scroll up, down, left, or right around x/y, inside the element named by container, or around the screen center when neither is given. Coordinates use logical points. pages moves exactly that many pages of the container (or the screen) and holds before lifting, so the list does not coast past items: use it for carousels and horizontal lists. Waits for the list to stop, then returns screen_change (unchanged means it did not move, as at the end of a list; unknown means it could not be compared), moved (the container whose items shifted, and by how much) and the visible text, so there is no need to look again.

device.description: The device to act on: its id from list_devices (or its exact name).

verify.description: Set false to skip action verification. Returns verified:false. Text targeting and coordinate sizing still read current device data.

container.description: Visible label of the scrolling list or row itself.

tools.name: scroll_to
tools.description: Search for visible text and scroll until it is found, content stops changing, or max_scrolls is reached. container (the label of the scrolling list) or x/y says which list to scroll; left and right move one page at a time without coasting, so items in a carousel are not skipped. The result names the container that moved. The default limit is ten scrolls and at most 50 are made; missing text is an error.

device.description: The device to act on: its id from list_devices (or its exact name).

container.description: Visible label of the scrolling list or row itself.

tools.name: drag
tools.description: Hold a touch, then move between the supplied logical-point endpoints. hold_seconds defaults to 0.6 and duration_ms to 800. Delivery does not prove a drop succeeded.

device.description: The device to act on: its id from list_devices (or its exact name).

tools.name: pinch
tools.description: Perform a two-finger gesture centered at x/y in screen points. scale above one spreads fingers; below one brings them together. Centers too close to an edge are rejected.

device.description: The device to act on: its id from list_devices (or its exact name).

tools.name: touch_path
tools.description: Draw one continuous stroke: touch down at the first point, pass through every point at its time_ms, and lift at the last point. Points are logical screen points, as in a screenshot; time_ms starts at 0 and strictly increases, with at most 8192 points and 60000 ms. Use it for a circle, a curve or any drag that is not a straight line. Points are sent as given, without smoothing or added timing. sent only means the touches were written; inspect the screen to judge the drawing.

device.description: The device to act on: its id from list_devices (or its exact name).

time_ms.description: Milliseconds after the stroke touches down, fractions allowed. 0 for the first point, then strictly increasing.

verify.description: Set false to skip reading the screen after drawing. Returns verified:false.

tools.name: draw_strokes
tools.description: Draw 1 to 12 separate strokes in one call. Each stroke touches down, passes through its points like touch_path and lifts before the next one starts. time_ms starts again at 0 in every stroke; each stroke has at most 8192 points, and the strokes together last at most 60000 ms. Use it for handwriting, a signature or a drawing made of several lines on a canvas that stays still between strokes. sent only means the touches were written; inspect the screen to judge the drawing.

device.description: The device to act on: its id from list_devices (or its exact name).

time_ms.description: Milliseconds after the stroke touches down, fractions allowed. 0 for the first point, then strictly increasing.

verify.description: Set false to skip reading the screen after drawing. Returns verified:false.

tools.name: type_text
tools.description: Enter text into the focused field, optionally clearing it first and sending Return after verification. An empty text with clear=true only clears. Unicode uses the clipboard; an unavailable snapshot means old contents cannot be restored. A system paste permission prompt raised by the input is answered with Allow Paste, and Return waits for the read-back. If the text cannot be confirmed, the result is an error with reason and instruction, and Return is not sent. submit_sent reports a key event, not a completed form.

device.description: The device to act on: its id from list_devices (or its exact name).

tools.name: fill
tools.description: Focus a field by ref, coordinates, or matching field label/placeholder/value/identifier, replace its text, and optionally submit after text verification. With none of these, it uses the only text field on screen, waiting up to five seconds for it. A fill whose text could not be confirmed in the field is an error that stops a batch, on a phone as on a simulator, and says what the field holds. On a simulator plain text switches the keyboard to en_US first so an input method cannot rewrite it. A field it cannot confirm as the target gets no text and returns an error. On a phone that includes coordinates with no field under them. Text fields with no id, the same name and the same text cannot be told apart, so fill refuses them: tap the one you want, then use type_text. Clipboard restoration can be unavailable. A system paste permission prompt raised by the input is answered with Allow Paste, and Return waits for the read-back.

device.description: The device to act on: its id from list_devices (or its exact name).

tools.name: press_key
tools.description: Send a named keyboard key with optional modifiers and count (default one). delete is backward deletion; forward_delete deletes ahead of the caret. Read back the field to verify edits.

device.description: The device to act on: its id from list_devices (or its exact name).

tools.name: hide_keyboard
tools.description: Detect a visible keyboard, use its unique visible accessibility hide key when available or send the toggle event, and verify dismissal. Does nothing when already hidden. Some emoji panels remain visible and are reported as an error without changing input methods.

device.description: The device to act on: its id from list_devices (or its exact name).

tools.name: press_button
tools.description: Send a hardware-style button event such as Home, lock, volume, mute, or Siri. Supported effects depend on the target platform.

device.description: The device to act on: its id from list_devices (or its exact name).

tools.name: system_gesture
tools.description: Send the requested system navigation gesture. Read back the display to check which system surface opened.

device.description: The device to act on: its id from list_devices (or its exact name).

tools.name: go_back
tools.description: Tap a uniquely identified back control when available, otherwise swipe from the left edge. The application decides whether navigation occurs.

device.description: The device to act on: its id from list_devices (or its exact name).

verify.description: Set false to skip action verification. Returns verified:false. Text targeting and coordinate sizing still read current device data.

tools.name: rotate
tools.description: Request a display orientation and invalidate cached coordinates. A rotation lock or missing orientation confirmation is reported as an error.

device.description: The device to act on: its id from list_devices (or its exact name).

tools.name: set_appearance
tools.description: Request light or dark appearance on the device. Unsupported device actions are returned as errors.

device.description: The device to act on: its id from list_devices (or its exact name).

tools.name: set_accessibility
tools.description: Change supported text-size or accessibility display settings. Some settings require manual Settings interaction or are unavailable on a particular OS; errors are preserved.

device.description: The device to act on: its id from list_devices (or its exact name).

tools.name: list_apps
tools.description: List installed applications, excluding system apps unless include_system=true.

device.description: The device to act on: its id from list_devices (or its exact name).

tools.name: launch_app
tools.description: Launch an application by bundle_id or unambiguous name. Optional language, locale, arguments, and environment affect launch. Physical-device launch uses the paired device AppService directly and verifies its returned PID against the observed foreground. Physical-device name lookup uses installed names and available localized Home Screen aliases, preferring an exact match then a unique case-insensitive substring; ambiguous matches require an explicit bundle_id. A per-device directory is shared across sessions for up to five minutes; misses or ambiguous cached results refresh once. Explicit bundle_id skips lookup. An app that is already running resumes where it was (resumed=true); fresh=true terminates it first. On a physical device the reply ends with the visible text, so a first-run sheet shows without another look. Name lookup requires the device streaming app-list service.

device.description: The device to act on: its id from list_devices (or its exact name).

tools.name: terminate_app
tools.description: Stop an application identified by bundle_id on the device.

device.description: The device to act on: its id from list_devices (or its exact name).

tools.name: install_app
tools.description: Install an application from a local path. Requires operator approval by default and valid Apple signing where applicable.

device.description: The device to act on: its id from list_devices (or its exact name).

tools.name: uninstall_app
tools.description: Remove an installed application identified by bundle_id. Requires operator approval by default; application data may be removed by the platform.

device.description: The device to act on: its id from list_devices (or its exact name).

tools.name: open_settings
tools.description: Open a supported Settings page or an application settings page. Routes vary by iOS version and some require visible navigation or manual interaction.

device.description: The device to act on: its id from list_devices (or its exact name).

tools.name: open_url
tools.description: Ask the device to open a URL. Requires operator approval by default; the device chooses the registered handler.

device.description: The device to act on: its id from list_devices (or its exact name).

tools.name: build_and_run
tools.description: Build an Xcode project or workspace from project_path, install the result, and launch it. scheme may be required for ambiguous projects; configuration defaults to Debug. Requires operator approval and platform signing when applicable.

device.description: The device to act on: its id from list_devices (or its exact name).

tools.name: set_location
tools.description: Start a simulated latitude/longitude for the device. The platform session owns the override until cleared or closed.

device.description: The device to act on: its id from list_devices (or its exact name).

tools.name: clear_location
tools.description: Stop the location simulation owned by this service for the device.

device.description: The device to act on: its id from list_devices (or its exact name).

tools.name: get_clipboard
tools.description: Read clipboard contents supported by the platform. Requires operator approval by default; returned contents may be private.

device.description: The device to act on: its id from list_devices (or its exact name).

tools.name: set_clipboard
tools.description: Replace the device clipboard with text. Requires operator approval by default.

device.description: The device to act on: its id from list_devices (or its exact name).

tools.name: list_crashes
tools.description: List available reports, optionally filtering by process name or bundle identifier and kind. Defaults to crash reports and a limit of 30.

device.description: The device to act on: its id from list_devices (or its exact name).

tools.name: get_crash
tools.description: Read a report by path from list_crashes, or find the newest report for process. Return a summary unless full=true. Symbolication uses only matching build UUIDs and architecture from this session.

device.description: The device to act on: its id from list_devices (or its exact name).

tools.name: download_app_container
tools.description: Copy an accessible application container to a local destination, or the service state directory by default. Requires operator approval and platform container access.

device.description: The device to act on: its id from list_devices (or its exact name).

tools.name: request_human_action
tools.description: Optional. Show a macOS dialog asking the user to complete reason on the device; no other tool requires it. Wait for an actual Done/Cancel response, up to timeout_seconds (default 300). Done is an acknowledgment; inspect the device before continuing.

device.description: The device to act on: its id from list_devices (or its exact name).

tools.name: handle_alert
tools.description: Choose a visible alert button by text or accept/dismiss action, waiting up to five seconds for it to appear. Ambiguous buttons are not tapped. Recognized prompts are reported by kind. For purchase prompts, generic accept does not tap and returns the kind and available buttons. Confirm a purchase only when the user explicitly requested it, by setting button to the visible button text. Generic dismiss and other prompt kinds remain available.

device.description: The device to act on: its id from list_devices (or its exact name).

tools.name: wait_for
tools.description: Poll visible text until it appears, or disappears when gone=true. timeout_seconds defaults to ten. Disappearance requires a complete readable result; unreadable or truncated content is not proof of absence.

device.description: The device to act on: its id from list_devices (or its exact name).

tools.name: wait
tools.description: Pause for seconds without interacting with the device. It runs in order with this session's other calls to that device.

device.description: The device whose calls this pause sits between: its id from list_devices (or its exact name).

tools.name: batch_commands
tools.description: Do a whole known task on one device in one call: launch the app, tap, fill, scroll, go back and answer alerts, up to 30 steps in order, each {tool, arguments}. Prefer this to separate calls whenever the request already names what to do. Every step is checked before any runs. Steps that tap wait up to five seconds for their target, so a batch can cross screens. The reply ends with the foreground app and the visible text, so no screenshot or second look is needed unless you need pixels. It stops at the first failure and reports the failed step, the closest text on screen and remaining_steps; fix that step and send only those. It also pauses before the steps that follow a tap after which no change was observed (same elements, text, values, state and positions), named in unchanged_step: those steps were written for the screen that tap should produce, and the batch cannot tell whether it did. That is not a failed tap; check screen in the reply, then send remaining_steps, with that tap first only if its effect is missing. A tap followed by another step aimed by coordinates (tap, double_tap, long_press, swipe, drag, scroll or pinch) is not compared, because such a run is written for one screen, so the batch does not pause there. stop_on_error=false continues past ordinary errors and compares no tap. A step with arguments.verify=true is always compared. Cancellation, timeout and unknown input always stop it. Nested batches are rejected and approval requirements still apply. Every step runs on the top-level device; steps carry no device of their own.

device.description: The device every step runs on: its id from list_devices (or its exact name).

verify.description: Set false to skip verification on supported steps unless a step overrides it. Read the final screen once; its snapshot does not verify each action.

tools.name: run_code
tools.description: Run JavaScript on an independent worker to do a multi-step device task in one call, deciding each next step from the results instead of returning to the model between steps. code is an async function body, or an async arrow function, that may read input (your JSON) and must return a JSON-serializable value. Call device tools with await tools.<tool_name>(arguments), each naming its device as a direct call does; only the devices listed in devices may be used, and the script holds those devices, and only those, while it runs; each returns the same structured result the tool would, so the code can inspect it, loop, filter, count and choose what to do next. Prefer one run_code for predictable multi-step work, such as scrolling until something appears and then reading it; use a single device tool directly for a one-step action, and return an image and the progress so far to the model when the next decision needs visual judgement rather than forcing a long fixed script. The sandbox exposes only tools, input and console: there is no require, file system, network, process or timer. A tool error throws and the code can catch it and adapt. An action receipt with sent=false or an unknown outcome stops the script and returns the steps already run, the same stop rule batch_commands uses; cancellation and timeout also stop it and cancel the device call in progress. The result reports every tool call with its name, elapsed time and receipt. Default limits are 120 seconds in total and 60 tool calls.

devices.description: Every device the script may act on: ids from list_devices (or exact names).

tools.name: acquire_device
tools.description: Exclusively occupy one device across tool calls in this MCP session. No boot occurs. A session may hold leases on several devices, one each; renew explicitly before expiry. Arbitration applies only inside this daemon.

device.description: The device to act on: its id from list_devices (or its exact name).

tools.name: renew_device
tools.description: Extend one of this session’s active device leases by 1–600 seconds (default 120).

tools.name: release_device
tools.description: Release one of this session’s device leases after cancelling this session's accepted work on that device and awaiting its recording/location cleanup. Work on the session's other devices carries on. Dispatched input is not undone.

tools.name: cancel_device
tools.description: Stop previously accepted work and background recording/location in this MCP session, including calls made without a lease: on one device when device or lease_id is given, otherwise on all of them. Optionally require the matching lease_id. Does not undo dispatched input or affect another session.

device.description: Limit the stop to this device (id from list_devices, or its exact name).

tools.name: observe_device
tools.description: Capture one image with its structured observation, non-reused element references and prompt check. AX and image are sequential, not atomic. Use before input and after unknown delivery.

device.description: The device to act on: its id from list_devices (or its exact name).
